svg.title: Board layout and wires
svg.desc: 30 x 70 perfboard cut on the head side: where each component sits on the 10 x 24 grid, and the same components with the wires and the star ground. Generated from electronics.py and wiring.py.
svg.text: Board · component side, head on the left, wheel axis at the bottom (row 01)
female sockets, with the rows of pins
XIAO and driver boards, on the sockets
phase A and B terminal block, four poles
pins in X07, X06, X05, X04
pins in K01, L01, M01, N01
single ground node: the negative of C1, in S02. One wire per branch from here.
XIAO USB socket: flush with the outer face of the head.
part removed by the cut: the board ends 1.38 mm past column C0.
fixing holes: only at the far end; those at the head go with the cut.
panel guides: they square the board from the side, they do not cover it. It goes in from above.
hole B05, to drill out to Ø2.7: the third screw, the one that holds the cut end.
2 · The wires, with the star ground
star ground: the wires leaving the node
power ground: lead of C1, − of C2
logic ground, local bus of its branch
at J4: the colour of the sensor cable (CAT5) wire on each pin - white-brown GND, brown VCC, green SCL, blue SDA
The star ground, as it is done here
The node is the negative of C1, in S02: its lead goes short to the driver power GND (O03).
THREE wires leave the node, and only three: to − of the 12 V block, to the driver logic GND (I02), to the XIAO GND (B08).
Each branch then has its own local bus, which touches no other: from the XIAO the sensor and LED ground,
from the driver logic GND, MS1 and MS2. No ground connects to another ground outside the node.
C2, if fitted, sits on the pins of the block: its − goes to − of the block, not to the node.
In brackets the hole: first as read FROM ABOVE, on the component side, then as read FROM BELOW, on the solder side.
3 · The same board seen FROM BELOW, on the solder side
The drawing is flipped the way the board is flipped; the letters still run left to right, because they are printed on this face too.
WARNING: the orientation of the XIAO (D0–D6 on row R8) comes from the maker's pinout turned with the USB
to the left; the old layout had it the other way round. Check it on the real XIAO before soldering.
Positions and wires come from mechanics/wheelly-cad/src/electronics.py and wiring.py: moving a component there moves
the check that it clears the box as well. The bodies of terminal blocks, headers and resistors are catalogue ESTIMATES.
The wires are drawn smooth, with a white halo at crossings to show which is on top. They say what goes where, not the route.
